name: Tsuyosa Automatic
alt: Citizen Tsuyosa NJ0150-56X with green dial and stainless steel bracelet
label: For your first automatic
intro: A little color. A lot of character.
why: The green dial and integrated bracelet give this three-hand watch a distinct personality. Consider it if you want a mechanical watch that can move from a workday to dinner without changing straps.
tradeoff: An automatic needs regular wear or winding. Choose a quartz or light-powered watch if you want to pick it up after weeks in a drawer and go.

name: Marlin Chronograph
alt: Timex Marlin chronograph with silver dial, dark subdials and steel bracelet
label: For the vintage look
intro: The charm of a different decade.
why: A silver dial, dark subdials and a domed crystal give the Marlin a vintage-inspired look. The quartz chronograph offers stopwatch functionality without the winding routine of a mechanical movement.
tradeoff: The acrylic crystal is part of the retro appeal, but it needs more care around scratches than sapphire. Check the model number: Marlin variants use different straps and movements.

name: Brycen Eco-Drive
alt: Citizen Brycen chronograph with ivory dial and brown leather strap
label: For a bigger presence
intro: A weekend watch with useful details.
why: The ivory dial, dark bezel and brown leather strap create a relaxed, sporty combination. Eco-Drive uses light to charge the watch, while a chronograph adds elapsed-time measurement.
tradeoff: At 44 mm, this is the largest watch in our starter selection. Compare the size with a watch you already wear, and consider whether you prefer a leather strap or bracelet.
